chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Abu Khalid al-Qammat, from Humran who said:
I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): What is the meaning of the words of God, Mighty and Majestic:

'For this reason We prescribed upon the Children of Israel that whoever kills a soul — except in retaliation for a soul or for corruption in the land — it is as if he has killed all people altogether'

He said: I said, 'And how is it as if he has killed all people altogether, when he has only killed one?' So he said: 'He will be placed in a place in Hell where the most severe punishment of its inhabitants reaches its peak — as if he had killed all people altogether, he would still only enter that same place.' I said, 'And if he kills another?' He said: 'It is doubled upon him.'

key_terms.شِدَّةُ عَذَابِ أَهْلِهَا: The severity of punishment of its inhabitants — denoting the most intense level of hellfire
key_terms.فَكَأَنَّمَا قَتَلَ النَّاسَ جَمِيعاً: As if he killed all people — the Quranic metaphor for the absolute gravity of unjust killing
key_terms.يُضَاعَفُ: It is doubled — each additional killing multiplies the punishment
key_terms.يُوضَعُ فِي مَوْضِعٍ مِنْ جَهَنَّمَ: He is placed in a specific location in Hell — signifying a reserved station of maximum punishment

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir explain about killing one soul being like killing all mankind (Quran 5:32)?
ai.summary: This hadith records Humran ibn A'yan asking Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (AS) about the exegesis of Quran 5:32, which equates killing one innocent soul to killing all of humanity. The Imam explains the verse's meaning through a description of the afterlife: the murderer is placed in the most extreme position of punishment in Hell — the same spot reserved for one who would have killed all mankind. If he kills another person, the punishment is further doubled. This teaching emphasizes that unjust killing carries cosmic moral weight in Islam's eschatological framework.

en.hubeali: Ali BIin Ibrahim narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ali Bin Uqba, from Abu Khalid Al Qammat, from Humran who said,
‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘What is the Meaning of the Words of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic
[5:32] For this reason did We Prescribe to the Children of Israel that whoever slays a soul, unless it be for manslaughter or for mischief in the land, it is as though he slew all the people.

I said, ‘And how come it is as if he has killed all the people, for he has (only) killed one?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He would be placed in a place of Hell where the harshest of Punishments would end up to be upon its inhabitants, had he killed the people altogether. But rather, he would enter that place’. I said, ‘So if he were to kill another one?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It would be doubled upon him’.
